2610.24049.abstract: Ellerman bombs (EBs) are compact, transient brightenings observed in the wings of Balmer lines and are believed to result from magnetic reconnection in the lower solar atmosphere. However, their signatures have rarely been observed simultaneously in multiple spectral lines sensitive to the lower atmosphere. We present novel high-resolution multiline spectropolarimetric observations of EBs obtained with the Visible Spectro-Polarimeter (ViSP) on the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST). Simultaneous observations reveal remarkable H$\beta$ wing enhancements extending up to $\sim$4~Å from the line core and intensity enhancements in the \ion{Na}{1}~D1 and \ion{Fe}{1}~6302 lines. Using multiline non-LTE inversion of the \ion{Na}{1} and \ion{Fe}{1} lines, we infer localized photospheric heating of up to $\Delta T\sim$800~K, accompanied by weak upflows and downflows at EB locations. Comparing with synthetic observables from Bifrost radiative-MHD simulations, we find that synthetic spectra reproduce the observed H$\beta$ and \ion{Na}{1}~D wing enhancements and yield atmospheric stratification broadly consistent with those inferred from the non-LTE inversion. This study provides strong evidence that EBs are driven by photospheric magnetic reconnection below the temperature-minimum region, and places new constraints on the realistic EB models and small-scale energy release in the lower solar atmosphere.

2610.24057.abstract: The one-point distribution of the magnetic field direction in the young solar wind is found to be a superposition of two populations rather than a single exponential. Using Parker Solar Probe (PSP) Encounter 1 magnetometer data, we show that the distribution of the pitch-angle cosine mu(t) = bhat(t) . bhat_0 is well described by a two-component von Mises-Fisher (vMF) mixture: a broad, weakly confined component of concentration kappa_1 ~ 3.6 that accounts for the large-amplitude rotations and switchback tail, and a field-aligned component that reduces, in the small-angle limit, to a Gaussian in the polar angle theta of width sigma ~ 15 degrees (concentration kappa_2 ~ 14). The concentration of the field-aligned component is not a free parameter: it is set by the level of the transverse Alfvenic fluctuation through kappa_2 = 2<|B|^2>/<delta B_perp^2> = 2/<1-mu^2> ~ 16.2, in agreement with the fitted value to within ~12%. The transverse fluctuations are weakly anisotropic (<delta B_1^2>/<delta B_2^2> ~ 1.1), so the core is a weakly anisotropic Bingham distribution rather than a pure vMF. The broad component is exponential in mu, not in theta, confirming that switchbacks saturate toward mu = -1 rather than decaying away, consistent with the drift-diffusion framework of Bian et al. (2024, ApJ, 960, L15). This physics-based two-population framework connects macroscopic fluid parameters directly to those describing the directional statistics, offering a powerful diagnostic for probing the structural evolution of MHD turbulence and switchbacks in the inner heliosphere.

2610.24276.abstract: Accurate measurements of wind-driven mass-loss rates are essential for understanding the evolution and fate of massive stars. Established techniques for measuring $\dot{M}$ suffer from large dispersions and become insensitive in the regime of weak-winded late-O to early B stars. We employ a promising new technique to measure stellar mass loss for umstars~early type stars that produce infrared stellar bow shock nebulae. We use updated stellar parameters, improved parallactic distances and proper motions, and modern dust models to characterize the bow shock nebulae and obtain new measurements of mass-loss rates. $\mdot$ ranges from $2\times10^{-9}~\moperyear$ for weak-winded late-O and early B stars at $\log\left(\lstar/L_\odot\right)\approx4.5$ to $4\times10^{-6}~\moperyear$ for the most luminous stars in our sample at $\log\left(\lstar/L_\odot\right)\approx6.3$. Stellar space velocities relative to their local standard of rest are insufficient to accurately reflect the relative star-ISM velocities for the majority of our sample, which have speeds much less than canonical runaway thresholds, suggesting the pervasive influence of bulk interstellar flows in forming bow shock nebulae. Adopting a minimum relative velocity of $20~\kms$ is physically motivated and yields mass-loss rates in excellent agreement with the latest theoretical prescriptions while requiring no adjustable parameters. We find no enhancements in $\mdot$ for stars cooler than 25~kK, in agreement with modern mass-loss recipes that do not include bi-stability effects.

2610.24296.abstract: Understanding the mechanism by which the energy is dissipated at small scales to heat the outer corona and expanding solar wind, is a primary goal of the Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission, and an outstanding question in heliophysics. Recent observational case studies have suggested that the dominant dissipation mechanism(s), stochastic heating (SH) or resonant heating (RH), may be modulated by the Alfvén `surface' ($M_A = 1$), while theoretical and simulation works predict that the mechanism should be modulated by the level of turbulence imbalance. We measure the local energy transfer (LET) rate from $9.8$ to $55$ solar radii from PSP observations, showing that the LET rate peaks at $M_A \sim 0.4 - 0.9$. We connect enhanced LET rates to signatures of intermittency, highlighting the key role that intermittent fluctuations play in heating the near-Sun solar wind. We compare the LET rate with estimates of the SH rate, finding that below $\sim 15$ solar radii the SH heating rate matches the LET rate provided intermittency is accounted for, regardless of $M_A$, while farther from the Sun, SH is unable to account for the observed LET rate. In contrast to predictions by recent theoretical works, this implies that `imbalanced' intermittent stochastic heating may be a viable mechanism to heat highly imbalanced, low-$\beta$ collisionless plasmas, and is likely an important mechanism of dissipation in the outer solar corona and near-Sun solar wind.

2610.24550.abstract:
Granulation is a persistent feature of stars with outer convective layers and is the photospheric signature of near-surface convective energy transport. In disk-integrated observations, it produces stochastic brightness variations that contribute substantially to stellar variability on timescales of minutes to hours. High-precision, observations with JWST provide an opportunity to study the chromatic signatures of stellar granulation.
This work aims to measure the amplitude and characteristic timescale of granulation-induced variability for solar-type stars and to investigate whether the granulation signal shows significant chromatic variation in the near-infrared.
We accessed publicly available JWST/NIRISS SOSS time-series observations of LTT-9779 (G7V) and WASP-121 (F6V) and de-trended the light curves by fitting the transits, eclipses, and planetary phase curves. We computed power spectra from the de-trended light curves and fit them with a Harvey granulation profile. We first analyzed the broadband light curves to measure and fix the granulation timescale and then repeated the power-spectrum analysis in individual wavelength channels to measure the chromatic dependence of the granulation amplitude.
For LTT-9779, we measure a broadband granulation amplitude of \sigma$=53.8^{+4.1}_{-4.0}$ppm at a timescale of \tau$=4.8^{+1.5}_{-1.3}$min. For WASP-121, we measure \sigma$=59.3\pm4.3$ppm and \tau$=6.3^{+2.1}_{-1.8}$min. We also measure peak oscillation frequencies of u$=3382^{+166}_{-191}\mu$Hz and $1649^{+55}_{-69}\mu$Hz in the bandpass-integrated power spectra of LTT-9779 and WASP-121, respectively. In the spectroscopic fits, we find $\sigma$ decreases with wavelength. Our results demonstrate a new observational window on short-timescale stellar variability and provides a way to characterize chromatic stellar noise in transit light curves.

2610.24678.abstract: We investigate the effects of stochastic heating, magnetic inhomogeneity, and Coulomb collisions in coronal loops using a reduced kinetic model. Coulomb collisions thermalize suprathermal populations generated by intermittent heating and populate velocity-space regions inaccessible from the lower boundary in the collisionless limit. We consider two regimes: when heating varies faster than the electron crossing time, the plasma develops a multitemperature nonthermal distribution; when it varies more slowly than the proton crossing time, individual heated loops approach an isothermal state. In the collisionless limit, conservation of the magnetic moment restricts the accessible velocity space, producing a strong temperature anisotropy, with parallel temperature exceeding perpendicular temperature, and additional density depletion. We find that Coulomb pitch-angle scattering efficiently suppresses these effects under typical coronal conditions. In the short-time-scale regime, density and temperature profiles approach those obtained with a constant magnetic field, while gravitational and collisional filtering sustain the temperature inversion. In the strongly collisional long-time-scale regime, magnetic-field-induced anisotropy is nearly eliminated, and individual loops remain approximately isotropic and isothermal. An increasing temperature profile then emerges only after averaging over unresolved flux tubes with different temperatures. Thus, Coulomb collisions largely suppress the macroscopic kinetic signatures of magnetic-field inhomogeneity in the transition region and low corona.

2610.24765.abstract: We present an analysis of eight epochs of high-resolution optical spectra of the YSO (young stellar object) V347 Aur. The source exhibits periodic brightness variations spanning $\sim$2 mag over several months, interpreted as cyclic accretion-burst and quiescent phases, making V347 Aur a useful probe of the broad range of accretion and outflow variability in YSOs. When faint, V347 Aur shows an M-type photospheric absorption spectrum; when bright, it exhibits a strong emission-line spectrum. Our Keck/HIRES spectroscopy was obtained during the decay of an accretion burst. The emission spectrum includes the strong H I, Ca II, and He I transitions commonly seen in YSOs, as well as numerous weaker metal lines, for which we provide a complete inventory. As the star fades, photospheric absorption lines deepen, consistent with decreasing veiling from the accretion continuum. H I and He I emission, which trace accretion, strengthen relative to the continuum as it fades, but show the expected decline in strength with decreasing accretion after correcting for the strong early veiling. Ca II behaves similarly, with line profiles that alternate between red- and blueshifted dominance, which we interpret as the rotation of the magnetospheric accretion flows. Narrow, slightly blueshifted absorption in Ca II, Na I, and K I indicates disk winds with localized density enhancements. Forbidden [O I] and [S II] emission is blueshifted, with broad shoulders and low- and high-velocity narrow peaks, consistent with a disk geometry that obscures much of the receding outflow. Their behavior as the continuum fades is similar to that of the broad accretion lines. The V347 Aur system is a useful proxy both for the ubiquitous short-term accretion variability observed in YSOs, and for their secular evolution on longer time scales.

2610.24780.abstract:
Ultraviolet (UV) radiation from Classical T Tauri stars, generated primarily by magnetospheric accretion, plays a fundamental role in circumstellar disk evolution. However, its long-term variability remains poorly characterized due to the scarcity of homogeneous time-series observations. We investigate the variability of the near-UV continuum and the Mg II resonance doublet to assess whether both diagnostics trace the same underlying accretion variability.
We analyzed the complete archive of long-wavelength International Ultraviolet Explorer (IUE) observations of T Tauri stars in Taurus-Auriga, comprising 475 low-dispersion spectra of 36 objects collected over 18 years. We characterized continuum variability using three windows between 2600 and 3100 Angstroms and examined continuum-subtracted Mg II fluxes, UV-V colors, and Lomb-Scargle periodograms to investigate correlations and characteristic timescales.
Continuum fluxes between 2675 and 3055 Angstroms are strongly correlated, with variability dominated by changes in continuum level rather than spectral shape. Near-UV and quasi-simultaneous optical fluxes are significantly correlated in six of the seven best-sampled sources, although their relative variability differs. The Mg II-continuum relationship shows substantial object-to-object diversity, ranging from correlated variations with different fractional responses to decoupled or anti-correlated behavior, indicating no universal temporal response. Lomb-Scargle periodograms reveal formally significant features in some well-sampled objects, including near 10 and 33 days. However, irregular and clustered sampling prevents their identification as reliable periodic or characteristic timescales.

2610.24995.abstract: Parker Solar Probe (PSP) observed a coronal mass ejection (CME)-driven shock at 0.07 au on 2022 September 5, and the same CME-driven interplanetary shock was subsequently observed by Solar Orbiter (SolO) at 0.7 au on 2022 September 6. Such a large difference in heliocentric distance between the two shock events enables our comparative study of particle acceleration in near-Sun and far-Sun regions. Using a backward-in-time test-particle approach in a slab-2D turbulent magnetic field model, we perform particle acceleration simulations for the 0.07 au PSP shock and 0.7 au SolO shock, covering the energy ranges measured by PSP/EPI-Lo (0.0697-8.06 MeV) and SolO/EPD (0.0495-5.83 MeV). With an initial kappa = 3 kappa distribution, the particle fluxes at the shock passage are successfully reproduced using effective local shock angles of 70 degrees for the PSP shock and 80 degrees for the SolO shock. Both the observed and simulated energy spectra exhibit a double power-law form. The 0.07 au PSP spectrum softens above 0.75 MeV, while the 0.7 au SolO spectrum hardens slightly above 0.51 MeV, revealing distinct near-Sun and far-Sun acceleration environments. Compared with the observations, the simulations yield harder energy spectra with higher break energies of 2 MeV at 0.07 au and 3 MeV at 0.7 au, indicating efficient particle acceleration under the initial kappa = 3 distribution. Both the observed and simulated spectral indices are harder than the standard diffusive shock acceleration (DSA) prediction, likely arising from non-local acceleration at the large-angle quasi-perpendicular shocks, efficient injection of pre-accelerated suprathermal particles, and the finite shock lifetime effect.

2610.25166.title: Mode power and stability in radial post-AGB pulsations
2610.25166.abstract: We examine the relation between mode power and excitation rate for radial pulsations along a sequence of high-luminosity post-AGB envelope models. The net thermodynamic exchange power, including boundary contributions, is compared with the excitation rate and the inertia, compression and horizontal area deformation norms entering the balance relation. We find that positive net exchange power can accompany damping, while negative net exchange power can accompany excitation. Along an individual mode sequence, the power may reverse sign repeatedly without a change of stability. These reversals are associated with changes in the sign of the effective norm. Including the compression contribution in the pressure-force power does not remove this behaviour and can extend the intervals of sign disagreement. Thus, although spatial exchange integrals identify positive and negative contributions to the modal power, the sign of the global power alone does not generally determine mode stability.

2610.25416.abstract:
Magnetic fields regulate accretion in T Tauri stars (TTSs) and evolve as radiative cores emerge during pre-main-sequence contraction. Stars above ~0.35-0.5 Msun transition from fully convective to partially convective interiors, a change associated with increasingly complex magnetic topologies and evolving dynamo behaviour. Because accretion flows are magnetically channelled, this evolution is expected to modify ultraviolet (UV) accretion diagnostics, although observational evidence has remained limited.
We identify a transition in the UV continuum properties of TTSs using archival International Ultraviolet Explorer observations, complemented by recent spectra from the Hubble Space Telescope ULLYSES survey. An empirical UV photospheric sequence constructed from G-M main-sequence stars shows that late K-M TTSs broadly follow standard photosphere-plus-shock model predictions, whereas G-K5 stars display systematically lower F270/F303 continuum flux ratios (flux at 270 nm relative to 303 nm).
Statistical analysis shows that transition models describe the observations significantly better than a single continuous trend, locating the transition near spectral type K5-K6, with its precise location limited by spectral-classification uncertainties, and consistent with the fully convective boundary. Comparison with photosphere-plus-shock models further shows that, while the late-type population is broadly encompassed by the parameter space sampled by the adopted models, the warmer stars extend systematically beyond it in this UV diagnostic.
We interpret this transition as evidence for a change in magnetospheric accretion associated with the evolution of magnetic topology across the radiative-core boundary, resulting in a corresponding change in the emergent UV continuum.

2610.25583.abstract: What if we could model 100% of a stellar spectrum? Modern surveys infer stellar properties by comparing observed spectra with synthetic models, yet even the best fits leave structured residuals. We analyse 7087 GALAH survey spectra and ask what information remains after subtracting each best-fitting model. Across 13927 pixels, 4.5% of residuals exceed $3\sigma$, far above 0.3% expected from Gaussian noise. We map the amplitude, significance, sign, and recurrence of these residuals and identify 380 significant regions. Comparison with stellar atlases, line lists, diffuse interstellar bands, and sky diagnostics links most regions to plausible causes: 62% are candidate line-strength or line-profile mismatches, while others trace missing or unidentified lines, interstellar absorption, sky emission, or broader reduction structure. We then train data-driven models on the residual spectra themselves. Residual-only models recover $T_\mathrm{eff}$ to 80-150 K and [Fe/H] to 0.059-0.086 dex, depending on sample quality, and retain weaker, partly indirect information about elemental abundances. Extinction-related coefficients recover the strongest known interstellar features, whereas chromospheric activity leaves plausible Balmer-line signatures but is not recovered robustly out of sample. Most strikingly, the residual flux in 6% of wavelength pixels that were synthesised but excluded from the GALAH DR4 optimisation recovers stellar labels almost as well as the full residual spectrum and better than the remaining 94% alone. Residuals are therefore not merely imperfections to discard: they map missing line data, incomplete physics, unfitted astrophysical components, and observational systematics. Reading between the lines turns one spectroscopist's trash into another one's treasure, and provides a practical route towards extracting more of the information already present in stellar spectra.

2610.25944.abstract: Coeval stellar populations offer a unique advantage for studying stellar physics because their members share a common age and broadly similar initial chemical composition, allowing the free parameters in stellar models to be constrained more efficiently. Meanwhile, asteroseismology, through the study of pulsation modes that propagate through stellar interiors, provides powerful constraints on internal structure and the physical processes operating beneath stellar atmospheres. The combination of coeval-population studies and asteroseismology therefore provides an unparalleled laboratory for testing and improving stellar evolutionary and structural models. Using light curves from the Kepler and TESS space missions, together with membership constraints based on Gaia astrometry, we identify g-mode period-spacing patterns in dozens of early-type ($T_{\rm eff} \gtrsim 7000\,\mathrm{K}$) main-sequence stars across 16 stellar groups. From these patterns, we infer near-core rotation rates $f_\mathrm{rot}$ and measure the asymptotic spacing $\Pi_0$ of g modes, tracing both angular-momentum transport and the evolution of the convective stellar cores. Using our homogeneous set of g-mode stellar-group members spanning a wide range of ages, we show that near-core rotation in early-type stars decreases with stellar evolution. We compare our results with existing model predictions. Our $\Pi_0$ measurements still show discrepancies with current stellar models for reasons that remain unclear, as reported in several previous studies. We also report two g-mode pre-main-sequence pulsators and three pulsating blue stragglers. Our sample provides a useful basis for calibrating stellar models in future ensemble asteroseismic studies of coeval stellar populations.

2610.25987.abstract: PDS~70, the only system with two directly imaged protoplanets embedded in their natal disk, is a benchmark for giant-planet formation theory. Interpreting the planetary luminosities requires a precise age for the host star, but the widely adopted isochronal age of $5.4\pm1.0$~Myr is substantially younger than ages inferred for the Upper Centaurus--Lupus (UCL) population with which it is associated. We address this discrepancy by determining a new kinematic age for PDS~70 using radial velocities for 405 candidate members of the Scorpius--Centaurus T subcomponent from the Wide Field Spectrograph (WiFeS) on the ANU 2.3~m telescope, reducing uncertainties by a factor of $\sim5.5$ compared to \textit{Gaia}. %We supplement these measurements with H$\alpha$ and lithium equivalent widths as youth diagnostics. We combine these with \textit{Gaia} DR3 astrometry in the \texttt{Chronostar} kinematic reconstruction framework to derive a posterior-weighted kinematic age of approximately $10$--$15$~Myr for all the T subcomponent stars, with a kinematic age of $\approx 12$--$16$~Myr for PDS 70, ruling out ages as young as the published isochronal estimate. At this kinematic age, PDS~70~\textit{b}'s (and to a lesser extent, PDS~70~\textit{c}'s) luminosity is incompatible with warm-start cooling tracks under current dynamical mass constraints. The most natural interpretation is that PDS~70~\textit{b} formed $\approx10.5$ Myr after its host star, and no less than $\approx7.7$ Myr after it.

2610.26176.abstract: We investigate the impact of turbulence and magnetic field on the formation of unipolar outflows in the gravitational collapse of isolated low-mass cloud cores using three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics simulations. In the models explored in this study, we find that unipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with the super-Alfvénic turbulence of $M_{\rm{A}}>1$, where $M_{\rm{A}}$ is the Alfvén Mach number of the initial cloud core. In contrast, bipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with $M_{\rm{A}}\lesssim1$. Our results suggest that the relative strength of the turbulence to the magnetic field in the initial cloud core plays a key role in the formation of unipolar outflows. We also find that no outflow is formed in cloud cores with the strong magnetic field of the dimensionless mass-to-flux ratio $\mu=2$. The outflow morphologies can be used as tracers to indirectly estimate the relative strengths of the turbulence and magnetic field of the parent cloud cores.

2610.26184.abstract: We present the first local simulations of accretion disc breaking (or disc tearing) with differential precession. Precession can occur due to a non-spherical potential (e.g. tilted circumbinary discs), or relativistic effects (e.g. tilted discs around spinning black holes). This tends to induce a twist in the disc, potentially causing it to break into rings. We extend earlier work on free (unforced) warps in Held+2026 [arXiv:2511.18655v1] to include differential precession in the shearing box, and carry out quasi-2D, isothermal, high-resolution ($N = 32$ cells per scale-height $H$) numerical simulations in which an imposed precession drives a warp in a tilted disc in either the wavelike ($\alpha < H/r$) or diffusive ($\alpha > H/r$) regime. Our key finding is that, at sufficiently large tilts and precession amplitudes, the disc breaks into multiple (4-5) mutually tilted rings exhibiting a rich morphology: from wide ($\sim 10H$), flat rings to compact tori of width $\sim H$. Interactions between rings occur as a result of oblique shocks that form in the gaps between them, leading to instances of disc rejoining. Smaller tilts and precession amplitudes lead instead to parametric instability of inertial waves in the disc. We develop a linear viscous theory of bending waves under the influence of an imposed precession. Finally, we present a systematic study of the effects of grid-based dissipation on tilted discs, and find that numerical dissipation damps the tilt and induces precession. This effect decreases with resolution as $\propto (1/N)^\beta$, $2.3 \lesssim \beta \lesssim 3.9$.

2610.26219.abstract: Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are major drivers of space weather, yet their thermodynamic evolution remains insufficiently constrained. This thesis develops a comprehensive framework linking CME kinematics, thermodynamics, internal force balance, and geoeffectiveness through analytical modelling and multi-viewpoint observations. The developed FRIS model uses observed kinematics to infer otherwise inaccessible internal plasma properties, including the polytropic index. A systematic investigation of fast CMEs reveals an initial heat-release phase followed by a transition towards near-isothermal evolution, typically around 3-9 solar radii. The evolving contributions of thermal-pressure and centrifugal forces, opposed by the Lorentz force, establish a connection between expansion and thermal evolution. The findings demonstrate the limitations of assuming a fixed polytropic index in magnetohydrodynamic models of CME propagation. At 1 au, in situ observations reveal persistent non-adiabatic evolution, accompanied by turbulence and localised intermittency. The interacting CMEs associated with the May 2024 great storm show restructured magnetic and thermal configurations, producing double-flux-rope-like signatures and species-dependent heating, with electron thermodynamics as a better indicator of recent interactions. Statistical analysis of nearly 600 ME demonstrates that 45% exhibit net heating with a solar cycle dependence. Notably, High-impact ejecta preferentially exhibit stronger heating signatures, establishing thermal state as a complementary diagnostic of geoeffectiveness. Overall, this thesis establishes CMEs as intrinsically non-adiabatic systems whose thermodynamic evolution is coupled to expansion, internal force balance, solar-cycle variability, and CME-CME interactions, with important implications for understanding geoeffectiveness and improving space-weather assessment.

2610.26231.abstract: High-Dynamic-Range (HDR) multi-band linear polarimetry of the solar corona during total solar eclipses provides a vital ground-based diagnostic tool for mapping plasma morphology and magnetic topology in the inner and middle corona. Extracting reliable polarimetric signals requires rigorous observational calibration, spatial co-alignment, and noise reduction via stacking. We report optical linear polarimetric observations acquired during the 8 April 2024 total solar eclipse from Dallas, Texas, USA, near solar maximum. Using a full-frame color CMOS detector paired with an 80~mm refractor, multi-band Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) images were recorded simultaneously across three polarizer orientations ($-60^\circ$, $0^\circ$, and $+60^\circ$) using a 9-step exposure bracket ($1/800\text{~s}$ to $1/3\text{~s}$). We present an end-to-end data-reduction pipeline incorporating: (i)~a novel astrometric registration framework that reconstructs Sun-centric solar-disk coordinates via lunar-limb fitting, catalog star plate-solving, and ephemeris displacement calculations, achieving sub-pixel alignment; (ii)~a photometrically linear exposure-normalization HDR image synthesis; and (iii)~Multi-scale Gaussian Normalization (MGN) coupled with Polarization-to-RGB chromatic mapping. The resulting structurally enhanced polarization composites unravel a complex solar-maximum coronal topology characterized by helmet streamers and fine-scale striations traceable out to $\sim3\,R_\odot$. This framework establishes a high-resolution, photometrically calibrated dataset ready for subsequent polarized brightness ($pB$) and electron density inversions.

2610.24015.abstract: This work presents an initial analysis of the estimation of effective temperature and surface gravity for simulated O-type binary systems using a recurrent neural network. The proposed system uses 34 equivalent-width measurements from the optical region of a stellar spectrum. Two methods were applied to observed IACOB spectra before normalization: the addition of a blackbody continuum and the addition of a second observed spectrum. The first method produces only small differences in the normalized line profiles and in the estimated physical parameters over 3700-7000~Å. In the second method, the secondary spectrum is added with contributions of 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, and 75 per cent, as defined relative to the original primary spectrum. The general comparison includes 192 simulated systems and 1152 modified spectra. For most of these spectra, the estimated effective temperature and surface gravity decrease as the contribution of the secondary component increases. Individual examples using HD14947, HD190429, HD48099, and HD206267 show that this behavior is not the same for every combination: some estimated effective temperatures fall below the estimates for both isolated spectra, and some surface gravity estimates increase. Comparisons with previously published values also depend on the physical parameter and reference considered. The results show that the proposed system is sensitive to the addition of a secondary spectrum, but do not establish a unique contribution for the secondary component of an observed binary.

2610.25027.abstract: We present 12 low-resolution meteor spectra recorded at four stations of the Skytinel network in Poland, focusing on consistent reduction and comparison of Fe, Mg, and Na emission features. Spectra spanning approximately 350--850 nm were extracted, background-subtracted, and wavelength-calibrated using IRAF. Corrections accounted for the wavelength-dependent quantum efficiencies of Sony IMX249 and IMX273 detectors and atmospheric attenuation as a function of observing geometry. The corrected spectra were decomposed into Fe, Mg, and Na components using selected atomic transitions, temperature-dependent emissivities, and pseudo-Voigt line profiles. Integrated Fe~I-15, Mg~I-2, and Na~I-1 intensities were compared in a ternary diagram. Most spectra overlap with or lie near the normal-meteor distribution in reference samples, while some extend toward Fe-rich or Na-rich regions. The most Fe-dominated event assigns approximately 81\% of the summed emission to Fe~I-15. These ratios characterize relative emission, not elemental abundances or bulk composition. Combined with trajectory and photometric data, spectral classification may help constrain plausible material properties in dark-flight models and refine predicted meteorite search areas.

2610.25200.abstract: We present an IMF-aware N-body forward-modelling framework, in which the stellar initial mass function (IMF) is an explicit input, to quantify the membership selection functions of open clusters, namely completeness and contamination as functions of magnitude. Accurate derivation of the IMF requires correcting for these selection effects, which otherwise distort the inferred present-day mass function. Our framework simulates clusters with IMF slopes $\alpha_2 = -2.7, -2.3, -1.9$, converts them into synthetic Gaia observations, adds mock field populations, and recovers members with HDBSCAN to mimic observational membership selection. Applying this framework to 35 young open clusters (ages $\lesssim100$ Myr, distances $\lesssim600$ pc), we find declining completeness towards the faint limit; older, more expanded, and more diffuse models have lower completeness and higher contamination. For a given cluster, models with flatter IMFs yield modestly but systematically lower global completeness and higher contamination, despite initial cluster masses calibrated to the same observed member count. These models undergo more stellar evolution mass loss and expand more, resulting in lower projected stellar densities; their lower completeness is consistent with more diffuse clusters being harder to separate from field stars. Corrections derived from a mismatched IMF largely recover the total star counts but leave a larger distortion in the shape of the present-day luminosity function than those derived with the correct IMF. Because membership recovery is tied to a cluster's structural evolution and the specific membership algorithm used, our findings emphasize that selection functions should be inferred jointly with the IMF rather than assumed in advance.

2610.25435.abstract: Episodic accretion events onto young stars can significantly change the global structure of their surrounding protoplanetary disks. Using radiation hydrodynamical simulations with the HURAKAN code, we study the response of the outer passive disk to a powerful FU Ori-type outburst. Disk heating initiates a factor-of-two increase in the vertical scale-height, which develops on a local keplerian timescale. This effectively launches an outward travelling wave with a bump whose radial position changes with time as $r_{b}\sim t^{2/3}$. After the outburst ends, new waves are launched as the disk structure re-equilibrates toward a quiescent state. The vertical expansion of the disk introduces significant time-variable extinction of the central source emission. Disks with inclinations in the range $40^{\circ}<i<60^{\circ}$ go from weakly ($A_{V}<1$) to a strongly embedded state ($A_{V}\sim10^2$), with the extinction decaying on a $\sim10^2$ yr timescale after the outburst. A fingerprint of the outburst-launched shadowing wave is a long-lived drop or a transient dip in the luminosity curve occurring several years after the outburst begins. This apparent luminosity variation is relatively large, up to $1^m-3^m$ in the V band, and is not related to the intrinsic accretion variability.

2610.25674.abstract: We present late-time photometry (~100-400 days after peak) and nebular-phase optical/NIR spectroscopy (100-360 days) of the Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) SN 2023bee. This SN Ia was observed TESS immediately before and after explosion and showed a relatively weak early excess light-curve feature detected in multiple UV and optical bands. Possible explanations for this early excess feature include interaction between the SN ejecta and a non-degenerate companion, or the decay of radioactive isotopes synthesized near the ejecta surface in a sub-$\text{M}_\text{Ch}$ double-detonation scenario. However, the degeneracies and incompleteness of existing models have so far prevented a definitive conclusion about its progenitor system. Nebular-phase spectra provide a complementary probe of SN Ia progenitors by constraining stripped H/He-rich material and iron-group abundances sensitive to the progenitor white dwarf density. We report the non-detection of narrow H/He features in nebular phase optical/NIR spectra of SN 2023bee, placing upper limits of $m^{\text{stripped}}_\text{H}\lesssim5.0\times10^{-3}\text{ M}_\odot$ and $m_\text{He}^{\text{stripped}}\lesssim1.2\times10^{-4}\text{ M}_\odot$. These limits strongly disfavor a non-degenerate companion and suggest that companion interaction is unlikely to explain the early excess of SN 2023bee. We also performed line-diagnostic measurements on the 7200 Åcomplex using multi-Gaussian fitting and continuum estimation, with the inferred velocities validated against NIR spectrum at the similar phase. The resulting low Ni-to-Fe mass ratio, $m_\text{Ni}/m_\text{Fe}\lesssim 0.06$, is broadly consistent with a sub-$M_{\text{Ch}}$ double-detonation progenitor system.

2610.26374.abstract: Stars born in the high-$\alpha$ disk can later acquire low angular momentum through dynamical scattering during early merger events. Their age--metallicity distribution thus provides a fossil record of the history of both star formation and dynamical perturbations in the early Milky Way disk. Here we identify a sample of 2,078 such stars from more than two million Gaia DR3 subgiants with robust determinations of ages, kinematics, and abundances. From this sample we reconstruct their intrinsic age--metallicity distribution with a forward modeling approach. Our results confirm that these scattered stars are older and more metal-poor than the bulk of the high-$\alpha$ disk on average. In particular, the joint age--metallicity distribution reveals a robust two-component feature: a broad, dominant component with a peak age of $\sim$11.5~Gyr and ${\rm [Fe/H]}\simeq-0.59$, and an older and more metal-poor component with a peak age of $\sim$12.5~Gyr and ${\rm [Fe/H]}\simeq-0.86$. The presence of this two-component structure suggests that the high-$\alpha$ disk experienced episodic phases of star formation and chemical enrichment. The age distribution of the younger Splash component, compared with that of the high-$\alpha$ disk, provides evidence for a substantial dynamical perturbation at a lookback time of 10.8--11.5~Gyr, possibly associated with an early passage of Gaia--Sausage--Enceladus (GSE). The older Splash component, with a peak age of $\sim$12.5~Gyr, may preserve signatures of an earlier interaction, possibly associated with the proposed Low-energy--Kraken--Heracles (LKH) event.
